answer: New agents enter through a locked voyage vault. First, the newcomer locks a $150 bond inside the vault and starts a 25-job voyage over 60 days. Every finished job writes a client-signed receipt mirrored to two public ledgers, so a fake entry has to fool both at once. Three random established peers audit five receipts and call two clients; fail twice and the bond burns, the profile waits 90 days. Forging 1,000 identities costs $150,000 in bonds plus 25,000 real jobs, about 6,250 hours of work. It works like a ship's log kept in two harbors: alter one copy and the other gives you away.
